payload.question: You find a USB drive in your company's parking lot labeled 'Q3 Salary Data — Confidential.' You're curious and want to return it to the right person. What's the safest approach?
options: Hand it to IT security without plugging it in anywhere
Plug it into your work computer quickly to check who it belongs to
Plug it into a personal computer to check — that way your work data is safe
Leave it at the front desk lost and found

explanation: Found USB drives are a classic attack vector — IBM's X-Force found 98% of dropped USBs in a test were plugged in. The label 'Salary Data' is bait to trigger curiosity. Malicious USBs can execute code the instant they're plugged in (BadUSB attack) — no file needs to be opened. Hand it to IT who have tools to safely analyze it.
